explanation: The L76V mutation reduces indinavir binding through an indirect allosteric mechanism: the loss of ~27 Ų of hydrophobic volume at position 76 creates a cavity in the C-terminal dimer region that destabilizes the local protein fold, propagating conformational changes that alter the geometry of the active site ligand-binding pocket despite the mutation being 8.2 Å away from the inhibitor. This local collapse likely increases the entropic cost of binding or shifts the protease conformation toward a less favorable state for accommodating indinavir's rigid core, as the decreased leucine side-chain contacts that normally stabilize the dimer interface are insufficiently compensated by the slightly more hydrophobic valine substitution.
